findings.problem: Development adapter printed password-reset, verification and invitation token links, recipient/account identifiers and preview links.
findings.change: Remove adapter console output and preview URL lookup; keep security links only in composed messages.

findings.problem: Development SMTP send failures were swallowed; partial rejected-recipient results resolved as complete success.
findings.change: Reject send failures in every mode and nonempty rejected-recipient reports. Do not retry sends automatically because accepted recipients may already have the message.

findings.problem: Invitation role/URL values interpolated into HTML; unsupported URL schemes accepted; raw configured frontend paths/query strings produced malformed action URLs.
findings.change: Validate HTTP(S) URLs without embedded credentials, escape HTML contexts, encode action tokens and derive app links from the configured primary origin. Preserve text links and existing welcome-admin sentinel semantics.
findings.impact_scope: Synthetic adapter-contract reproductions; no demonstrated public endpoint HTML-injection exploit. Invitation role/URL normally originate in server-controlled enum/configuration.

findings.problem: Concurrent first-use development sends could create multiple Ethereal accounts/transports and observe different initialization results.
findings.change: Cache one initialization promise, share its success/failure and reset it on initialization failure so a later call can retry.

findings.problem: Non-development sends without SMTP_HOST constructed a transport with implicit host fallback.
findings.change: Require a nonblank trimmed SMTP host before transport construction. Full SMTP configuration validation remains open.

open_followups.scope: SMTP port/secure/auth/sender inputs still read raw process.env; Number(port)||587 can hide invalid configuration. Config plugin omits these keys. Review explicit TLS/timeouts, environment defaults and typed composition during API plugin/container review. Adapter source stays open.
Real local SMTP capture/provider execution remains planned, not executed. Mocked submission and composition tests do not replace this lane or prove inbox delivery.

Register/invite/accept use background sends or catches; newsletter catches send errors after subscription/promotion persistence. Those workflows, outbox/retry policy, coupon generation/customer logging and raw provider-error logging remain owning-module work.

limits: No auto-resend or durable/outbox/exactly-once guarantee. Initialization retries differ from delivery retries. Partial rejection can follow successful submissions for other recipients.
Promises model transport submission only; successful transport responses do not prove delivery to an inbox.
Only adapter logging is removed. Caller logging and SMTP-provider error redaction are not globally certified.
Development still lazily uses Ethereal by existing mode policy; tests never contact it. Production/test now require configured SMTP_HOST for actual sends.

App links normalize to root routes on the configured primary HTTP(S) origin; invitation URLs preserve their provided path/query after URL normalization. No frontend deployment/base-path or complete authentication endpoint test.
Four port/facade/test files close; adapter and newsletter remain open for configuration/capture and owning-module policy. P01 remains open.
No DB/schema/provider execution or broad backend coverage remeasurement. Prior PostgreSQL 47-group evidence remains historical; P15 build/bootstrap checks remain open.
